title: Sequential limits along epimorphisms on a weakly contractible object
statement:
Let $(F_n,t_n)$ be an inverse sequence of sheaves of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with
epimorphic transition maps, and let $W$ be a weakly contractible object. Then every
$t_n(W)\colon F_{n+1}(W)\to F_n(W)$ is surjective, and for every $m$ the projection
$(\varprojlim_nF_n)(W)\to F_m(W)$ is surjective.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective], each epimorphic transition is locally surjective. Apply the definition [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible] at W to obtain surjectivity of each transition on sections, in the stated universe. No projective-representable equivalence is needed because hW is already this evaluation property.

source.place: First sentence: surjectivity of t_n(W) is part 3 of the weak-contractibility equivalences

proof.text: Fix m and a section a at stage m. Write G for the set-valued diagram obtained by evaluation at W. Define x_0 = G(0 <= m)(a). Recursively define x_(n+1) as G(n+1 <= m)(a) when n+1 <= m, and otherwise as a chosen preimage of x_n under the surjective adjacent transition. This is natural-number recursion on sets, using classical choice only for preimages, not choices of sheaf morphisms.

source.place: Middle sentence: successive lifts above m, with the dependent-choice construction expanded as chosen preimages and recursion

proof.text: For n <= m, the recursion gives x_n = G(n <= m)(a), so x_m = a. For n+1 <= m, adjacent compatibility is functoriality of G; otherwise it is the chosen-preimage equation. Induction on k <= n then gives compatibility for every transition n to k. Thus the x_n define a section of the diagram G. This also handles m = 0 and does not assume any section set is inhabited independently of a.

source.place: Middle sentence: earlier stages determined by descending transition maps; verify compatibility in both index ranges

proof.text: Use the sectionwise limit formula [det-pe-replete-definition]: evaluation at W preserves the limiting cone of F. Mathlib Types.isLimitEquivSections identifies its cone point with compatible tuples of G, and Types.isLimitEquivSections_symm_apply identifies its projections with tuple evaluation. Apply the inverse equivalence to the tuple from steps 2-3; its m-th projection is x_m = a.

source.place: Final sentence: sectionwise inverse-limit description and its coordinate projection

proof_origin.place: Entire proof; direct weak-contractibility evaluation and the existing epi/local surjectivity criterion, explicit natural-number recursion with prescribed earlier coordinates, induction on transition length, and the sectionwise limit equivalence. Formalized by G2, 2026-10-19.
